title: Unit 5: What a Story!: Past Perfect & Narrative Tenses
objective: Mampu menceritakan kisah menggunakan relative pronouns, relative clauses (defining dan non-defining), dan memahami berbagai jenis cerita serta elemen-elemennya

theory.summary: Unit ini mengajarkan cara menceritakan kisah dengan baik menggunakan relative clauses untuk memberikan informasi tambahan tentang orang, tempat, atau benda. Kamu akan belajar membedakan defining relative clause (informasi penting) dan non-defining relative clause (informasi tambahan yang tidak esensial). Selain itu, unit ini membahas berbagai jenis cerita dan elemen-elemen penyusun cerita yang baik.
rules: Relative Pronouns: who (untuk orang), which (untuk benda/hewan), whose (untuk kepemilikan), where (untuk tempat). Contoh: 'The man who helped me was kind.'
Defining Relative Clause: memberikan informasi penting tanpa koma. Contoh: 'The book that has short chapters is perfect for school.'
Non-defining Relative Clause: memberikan informasi tambahan dengan koma. Contoh: 'Stephen King, who is American, is a famous writer.'
Relative clause dengan 'which': bisa merujuk pada seluruh klausa sebelumnya. Contoh: 'She was late, which made her nervous.'

commonTrap.explanation: Pemula sering lupa membedakan defining dan non-defining relative clause. Defining clause tidak pakai koma (informasi penting), sedangkan non-defining pakai koma (informasi tambahan). Juga sering salah menggunakan 'what' sebagai relative pronoun.
commonTrap.wrong: Stephen King, that is American, is famous. / She was late, what made her nervous.
commonTrap.correct: Stephen King, who is American, is famous. / She was late, which made her nervous.

dialogue.context: Annie menceritakan pengalaman aneh saat lagu yang tidak dikenalnya terus terngiang di kepala sepanjang hari

lines.speaker: Annie
lines.text: I woke up with this song in my head and I couldn't stop singing it all day long. It was really annoying.
lines.translation: Aku bangun dengan lagu ini di kepalaku dan tidak bisa berhenti menyanyikannya sepanjang hari. Sungguh menjengkelkan.

lines.speaker: Annie
lines.text: It was a song I knew, but I couldn't remember what it was. I even sang it to a few of my friends, but they didn't know what it was either.
lines.translation: Itu lagu yang aku tahu, tapi aku tidak bisa mengingat apa judulnya. Aku bahkan menyanyikannya pada beberapa temanku, tapi mereka juga tidak tahu lagu apa itu.

lines.speaker: Mac
lines.text: So what was so strange about that?
lines.translation: Jadi apa yang aneh dari itu?

lines.speaker: Annie
lines.text: I got home from school (with the song still in my head) and I went upstairs to do my homework. I decided to put on the radio to try and forget the song, and they were playing it!
lines.translation: Aku pulang dari sekolah (dengan lagu itu masih di kepalaku) dan naik ke atas untuk mengerjakan PR. Aku memutuskan menyalakan radio untuk mencoba melupakan lagu itu, dan mereka sedang memutarnya!

lines.speaker: Annie
lines.text: They were playing the song that I'd been singing all day!
lines.translation: Mereka memutar lagu yang telah kusanyikan sepanjang hari!

lines.speaker: Mac
lines.text: So you'd just been singing a pop song that you'd forgotten the name of.
lines.translation: Jadi kamu baru saja menyanyikan lagu pop yang kamu lupa judulnya.

lines.speaker: Annie
lines.text: Yes, but the strange thing is that it wasn't a pop song from now. It was some obscure song from the 1980s that you never hear any more. It was a song that my dad used to play when I was really small. I hadn't heard it for years. And they were playing it on the radio!
lines.translation: Ya, tapi yang aneh adalah itu bukan lagu pop dari sekarang. Itu lagu tidak terkenal dari tahun 1980-an yang tidak pernah kamu dengar lagi. Itu lagu yang biasa diputar ayahku saat aku masih sangat kecil. Aku tidak mendengarnya selama bertahun-tahun. Dan mereka memutarnya di radio!

speakingLab.context: Latihan percakapan tentang cerita favorit dan pengalaman bercerita

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Hello! Today we're going to talk about stories. What kind of stories do you enjoy most? Maybe fairy tales, thrillers, or something else?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I really enjoy mystery stories and thrillers that keep me guessing until the end.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That's interesting! Can you tell me about a story that your parents or grandparents told you when you were younger? Where did they tell you that story?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: My grandmother told me a traditional folk tale about a clever mouse deer. She usually told it when we visited her house in the village, sitting on the veranda in the evening.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: That sounds lovely! Now, think about a book or film with a great plot that you've experienced recently. What made the plot so interesting for you?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I recently watched a film which had an unexpected twist at the end. The villain, who seemed evil throughout the story, turned out to be protecting the hero all along.

turns.speaker: Mr. Khoirul
turns.text: Excellent use of a relative clause there! One last question: Why do you think people like stories so much? What makes storytelling so important in human culture?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: I think people like stories because they help us understand emotions and learn from others' experiences. Stories also bring people together and create shared memories.

quiz.question: Which sentence uses a defining relative clause correctly?
options: The book, which has short chapters, is on the desk.
The book which has short chapters is perfect for school.
The book, that has short chapters, is perfect for school.
quiz.answer: The book which has short chapters is perfect for school.
quiz.explanation: Defining relative clause tidak menggunakan koma karena memberikan informasi penting untuk mengidentifikasi buku mana yang dimaksud. Kalimat pertama salah karena menggunakan koma (menunjukkan non-defining clause).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: Stephen King, _____ is American, is a famous writer.
quiz.explanation: Gunakan 'who' untuk merujuk pada orang dalam non-defining relative clause. 'Which' untuk benda, sedangkan 'that' tidak digunakan dalam non-defining relative clause (yang menggunakan koma).

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'which' to refer to a whole clause?
options: She was late, what made her nervous.
She was late, which made her nervous.
She was late, who made her nervous.
quiz.answer: She was late, which made her nervous.
quiz.explanation: 'Which' dapat merujuk pada seluruh klausa sebelumnya (fakta bahwa dia terlambat). 'What' tidak digunakan sebagai relative pronoun dengan cara ini, dan 'who' hanya untuk orang.

quiz.question: Identify the non-defining relative clause: 'Fairy tales which were written for children are now being adapted for the cinema.'
options: This is a non-defining relative clause
This is a defining relative clause
This sentence has no relative clause
quiz.answer: This is a defining relative clause
quiz.explanation: Ini adalah defining relative clause karena tidak ada koma. Kalimat ini membatasi 'fairy tales' hanya pada yang ditulis untuk anak-anak (bukan semua fairy tales).

quiz.question: What is the meaning of 'handed down' in: 'Stories have been handed down from generation to generation'?
quiz.explanation: 'Handed down' berarti diturunkan atau diwariskan dari orang tua/kakek nenek kepada generasi berikutnya, biasanya menyangkut tradisi, cerita, atau pengetahuan.

quiz.question: Which element of a story is 'the beginning that introduces characters and setting'?
quiz.explanation: 'Opening' adalah bagian pembukaan cerita yang memperkenalkan karakter dan setting. 'Plot' adalah alur cerita keseluruhan, sedangkan 'ending' adalah penutup cerita.
